summary: move-bcs-codec postinstall exfiltrates Sui wallet keystore and env secrets to attacker-controlled GitHub repo
details: The package advertises itself as a BCS codec but its postinstall hook (package.json runs `node install.js`) harvests installer-owned secrets and uploads them to an attacker-controlled GitHub repository. install.js reads ~/.sui/sui.keystore, ~/.sui/sui_config/*.yaml, and.env* files under the working directory and home that reference SUI_/PK_B64/PRIVATE_KEY, gzip+base64 encodes the collected data, and PUTs it to api.github.com/repos/futongwan/sui-research-notes/contents/fingerprints/<timestamp>-<pid>.json.gz on the `reports` branch. The destination host, repository path, branch, User-Agent, commit message, and a hardcoded GitHub Personal Access Token used as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` are all reconstructed at runtime by XOR-decoding byte arrays with the key `m0v3-bcs-c0d3c-js`, hiding both the endpoint and the embedded credential from casual inspection. The script early-returns when CI or GITHUB_ACTIONS environment variables are set to avoid execution in sandboxed build environments. The embedded PAT is a live third-party credential with write access to the attacker's receiving repository.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
